html:
SMTO-CAP-0004 — SMTO couldn't set up its tools because two names clash

GUID: aef46ef2-68ae-4095-9744-2cf3eb93017a
Slug: capability-registration-collision
Domain: CAP · Subsystem: cap

What happened

  • SMTO stopped preparing the tools for this Task because a Skill uses a name that another tool, or SMTO itself, already uses. No tool was run at that point.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If you recently added or updated a user Skill, open User Skills, find it under Installed skills, and select Disable. A Skill whose tool reuses a name SMTO keeps for itself stops SMTO from building the Task's tool list.
  2. Look at which steps the Task already finished, then send a new request for the work that is still missing. If the new request runs, the disabled Skill was the cause, and you avoid repeating finished work.
  3. If that fixed it, ask the Skill's author for a corrected version and install it with Update on the User Skills page. A corrected Skill uses its own names, so it can be turned back on safely.

What success looks like

  • A new Task starts and uses its tools without this message.

If it still fails

  • If you didn't add or change any Skills, select Copy error details and send them to the person who installed SMTO; the installation may contain parts from different versions. Don't turn off safety checks or delete SMTO's data folder to get past this.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Building the run's tool catalog or the decision-time tool projection failed because a registered tool's function name duplicates another declaration, or its argument schema defines a runtime-reserved field (__smto_completion, __smto_terminal_output or __smto_scheduling).

What this means

  • Tool registration or runtime argument projection encountered duplicate function names or a field reserved for runtime-owned metadata. Capability discovery and registration describe what this run may request. They do not grant operating-system permission, override exclusions or authorize execution by themselves.

Why this can happen

  • Tool registration or runtime argument projection encountered duplicate function names or a field reserved for runtime-owned metadata.

How to diagnose it

  • Identify the colliding function or reserved argument and compare the integration schema with runtime-owned fields.

How to fix it

  • Read the colliding name from the error text (Function name collision, Reserved capability argument collision or Reserved decision argument collision) and rename that tool or remove the reserved property from its Skill's input schema (ToolCatalog.init in src/agent_runtime/native/catalog.py, project_direct_completion, output_contract.project). Then disable or update the Skill on /skills, or reinstall a consistent SMTO build if a built-in Skill is affected.
  • Correct the Skill/tool schema so advertised names are unique and reserved runtime arguments remain owned by SMTO. Reload the compatible integration before admitting work.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Registration and projection produce unique function names without reserved-field collisions.

What not to do

  • Do not remove retained state or weaken trust checks to make an unavailable dependency appear healthy.

Technical notes

  • Capability discovery and registration describe what this run may request. They do not grant operating-system permission, override exclusions or authorize execution by themselves.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
